title: What Thought-Controlled Games Is
definition: Thought-Controlled Games: games played entirely by thought.
description:
Thought-Controlled Games: games played entirely by thought. This is Future Entertainment & Play at its most ambitious — neural inputs research, game logistics engineering and intent mapping operations converging on a single goal: making game hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Entertainment & Play will decide calibration outcomes this century. Thought-Controlled Games is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working game hulls, the larger neural inputs vision stalls, and with it, the game logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Thought-Controlled Games in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Thought-Controlled Games
definition: Today's documented research behind Thought-Controlled Games.
description:
The road to Thought-Controlled Games is already being paved. Virtual concerts (Fortnite, Roblox) draw tens of millions of simultaneous attendees. Location-based VR (Sandbox VR, Zero Latency) scales shared immersive play.

AI-generated music and video tools (Suno, Runway heritage) compress production. Together these programs form the neural inputs foundation that Thought-Controlled Games will build on — the game logistics results, the intent mapping methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as game logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Thought-Controlled Games
definition: Estimates Thought-Controlled Games readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Thought-Controlled Games components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a game hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Thought-Controlled Games operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Thought-Controlled Games installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 71929 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where neural inputs monitoring, game logistics redundancy, or intent mapping maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Thought-Controlled Games Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Thought-Controlled Games: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Thought-Controlled Games — games played entirely by thought.

Phase 1 — Prove (neural inputs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (game logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (intent mapping): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (calibration): game hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and gamers-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
